severityRationale:
Low CONFIRMED, but the script-auditor's stated basis - 'consistency with ledger eda17642 (Low)' - is NOT a severity argument and is DISCARDED. Consistency with a prior label cannot justify a label; the finding is re-argued on its merits and lands in the same place on stronger ground.

THE MEDIUM CASE, stated at its strongest: the rehearsal's one job is to be a faithful mirror that catches a mainnet cutover misconfiguration before it ships. The four-run controlled experiment (spot-reproduced by this classifier: CONTROL_EXIT=0 / BROKEN_EXIT=0 / BROKEN_WITH_PROBE_EXIT=1 'Uniboost: nudgeStreamer unset' / PRISTINE_WITH_PROBE_EXIT=0, break patch a single-line comment-out at :1736) proves the detector is genuinely gone, not weakened. The misconfiguration it detected reverts EVERY mint on indices 1/2/3 on mainnet, which is a protocol-availability impact and is exactly the C4 Medium shape.

WHY IT IS NOT MEDIUM. C4 Medium requires the protocol's function or availability to BE impacted, or value to leak under stated assumptions with documented external requirements. Here the availability impact is not caused by this defect - it is caused by a DIFFERENT, hypothetical operator error that has not occurred - and reaching it requires that error to ALSO evade the mainnet path's own detector. This classifier verified directly (not via subagent report) that the mainnet cutover script carries an explicit bidirectional wiring assertion phase: script/archives/DeployMainnetPromotionReady.s.sol:2455-2465 require()s nudgeStreamer() read-back on newUniboostEYE/SCX/FLX, the pooler, the ratchet, the SYA and the batch minter, each with a named failure string. A missed setNudgeStreamer therefore aborts the mainnet cutover LOUDLY at Phase 7 regardless of what the local mirror did. The deleted local mint was a redundant EARLIER layer of the same check, not the only one. Compounding this: the mainnet cutover the impact story invokes has ALREADY EXECUTED (fork @25949772 shows PhlimboV2 paused with totalStaked()==0, i.e. Phase 4e completed), and its script now sits in script/archives/ with its promotion-ready:dry / :broadcast npm keys deleted (ledger 3b7430a7, wont-fix). So the Medium framing rests on a FUTURE cutover, run from a script not currently wired, which would owe its own Phase-7-equivalent assertions whether or not this rehearsal exists.

That is a chain of hypotheticals, and C4 High/Medium explicitly exclude hand-wavy hypotheticals. What was actually lost is one layer of pre-flight assurance in a throwaway-chain rehearsal: real, reproducible, cheaply fixed, and correctly labelled Low. Overstating it to Medium would dilute the report - an explicit pipeline-rejection criterion. Law 1 is satisfied because nothing is dropped: the finding is reported at Low with a one-line executable fix.

TRIAGE PRIORITY 3 (highest of the non-regression, non-Law-2 items). It is the only finding in the run whose mechanism is proved by execution rather than inference, and its mitigation (the read-back require matching the SYA idiom at :1267) is one line and is independent of every other finding here.
